rules.finding: One Senator elected by highest vote total/plurality; state canvassing board resolves equal highest by lot, including a post-recount tie for a state-canvassed office outside the executive department. No runoff or primary nomination threshold is applied to the general Senate outcome.

For more than500votes cast and one candidate elected, losing margin of1percent or less of votes received by highest candidate entitles recount, subject to waiver. This is not1percent of all ballots or total contest votes. State-filed candidates' recount begins9AM fifthWednesday after election, December2,2026.

Outside automatic margin, losing candidate may request certified recount with payment within third day after canvass concludes. Cost initially100dollars per precinct voting in contest, actual-cost adjustments/refund rules retained in full statute. State-filed requested recount uses fifthWednesday or sixthWednesday if fifth cannot be used.

County must post convening notice before noon following election; canvass begins after early counting and at least24hours after notice. Obvious certification errors may be corrected with signed explanation. County abstract due thirdMonday November23; electronic/fax original due fourthWednesday November25. State board meets fourthMonday November30 and may adjourn until returns complete. Neither ENR Fully nor these meeting dates establishes that no eligible ballots remain.

Nebraska chapter provides election-contest grounds/procedures but32-1102 lists specified state offices and32-1109 concerns political subdivisions. Do not automatically apply their40day/20day venue deadlines as a U.S.Senate contest deadline. The U.S.Senate judges its members' elections/returns/qualifications. Complete later litigation/venue review remains external qualification.

Central areas8AM-8PM local; Mountain areas7AM-7PM local. Voters in line at closing may finish. Nebraska boundary is legally defined, including a section/range route through Cherry and county boundaries farther south; municipality boundary rule applies. Eastern priority counties including Douglas/Lancaster/Sarpy/Adams/Madison are Central; western Dawes/BoxButte/ScottsBluff/Cheyenne/Kimball/Keith/Chase/Perkins are Mountain. Cherry spans both; do not assign whole-county source timestamps a zone or infer exact per-native time zones. In November after DST ends, both ordinary closes correspond to02:00UTC November4, absent an operative extension.

Ordinary early ballots must be received by local close of polls; postmark alone is insufficient. Complete/sign oath, seal envelope, return to issuing county by mail/delivery. Ballot must not be dropped at a polling place as an assumed valid return route. Ballot request deadline is close of business secondFriday October23; in-office early voting runs from October5 through day before election under32-942 and the calendar. Agent pickup by onehour before polls close, return by closing, under32-943. No exact outstanding Senate votes follow from requests/envelopes.

Mail application requires Nebraska license/stateID number, copy of acceptable photoID, or reasonable impediment certification; missing/unverified applicationID prevents issuance pending provision. Return oath must be signed.32-1027 requires signature presence and registration/address checks; matching of reasonable-impediment certification signature is explicit. Do not invent a universal comparison/cure rule for every ordinary envelope. Provisional photoID cure is in-person by TuesdayNovember10; reasonable-impediment certification has its own verification requirements. No general post-election ordinary-envelope signature-cure extension was demonstrated.

Early counting board duties/envelope preparation may begin secondFriday before election. Counting may begin no earlier than24hours before polls open, at county discretion. No results may be released before polls close. These permissions are not county-specific observed batch timing.

Ordinary provisional eligibility requires registration/residence, correct precinct, signed documents, no duplicate vote and applicable primary-affiliation checks. Verification/investigation within7business days. ID-provisional review is distinct from ordinary provisional; count only once. No exact Senate remainder inferred from a provisional envelope count.

authority: SOS Military Voters and voterID guidance
rules.finding: Eligible military/overseas ballot requests may use FPCA, with same-calendar-year scope; thirdFriday request deadline,45day transmission, special60day ballot on written request, FWAB permitted for all elections. Receipt/return by methods authorized by SOS; do not assume unrestricted email return or a postmark/late-arrival grace period. Outside-Nebraska UOCAVA voters are exempt from ordinary photoID requirements; in-person Nebraska polling-site voting is different. Emergency responders outside county have a separate noon-electionday request route and authorized transmission. No currently operative Nebraska-specific court order extending ballot receipt was established by this bounded audit; comprehensive later docket coverage remains unproved.

Write-in affidavit/fee deadline secondFriday before election (October23), with qualification and name-mark rules; defeated-primary and withdrawn-writein restrictions remain. Generic marks are not automatically eligible votes. ENR does not display writeins; official canvass can retain scattering subject to source rules. Current roster is a five-named-choice publication, not proof that all eligible writeins/later changes are known.

Official19page opinion reverses/remands for mandamus requiring Burbank's inclusion as a Democratic candidate on May12primary ballot after untimely filing objection. This is primary-specific and does not put her on November's five-choice final publication. Opinion cites then-operative2025 filing law; laterLB1075 amendments and general roster remain separate.
